subject: physics
question_text: Derive an expression for the variation of acceleration due to gravity (a) above and (b) below the surface of the earth.

verification.note: The mark split is invented and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. The question itself is sourced, not invented.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: Above the surface
lines: On the surface g = G M / R². At a height h above
it the distance from the centre becomes (R + h):

steps.why: The factor 2 comes from expanding a SQUARE — it is the sign that this is the height formula and not the depth one.
common_mistakes: Dropping the factor 2, which is exactly what turns this into the depth formula.

recall.must_convey: That g at height h is G M by R plus h squared, giving g into one minus two h by R for small h.
accept: G M by R plus h squared
g into one minus two h by R

steps.label: Below the surface
lines: At a depth d only the sphere of radius (R − d)
below you pulls; the shell above pulls equally
in all directions and cancels. With uniform
density ρ, M = (4/3)πR³ρ, so g = (4/3)πGRρ and
steps.why: The two results differ in shape: above the surface g falls as an inverse square, below it falls in a straight line to zero at the centre.
common_mistakes: Using the whole mass M of the earth at a depth d, instead of only the mass below.

recall.must_convey: That only the sphere below pulls, giving g at depth equal to g into one minus d by R.
accept: g into one minus d by R
reject: g into one minus two h by R
